title: Is your group really a cooperative? Principles, form and bylaws

say: Is your group really a cooperative? Principles, legal form and bylaws.
This is the video for module one of Cooperative and Group Enterprise Management.
Many groups call themselves a cooperative. Some truly are. Others are one strong person's business with friends helping.
The International Cooperative Alliance, the global body for cooperatives, sets the standard. A cooperative is autonomous. A donor or buyer may support it, but does not control it.

panel.heading: A cooperative is people, not capital
items: Persons, not money, own the decisions
Voluntary: nobody is forced to join or stay

say: It is an association of persons. The member with the biggest share does not own more of the decisions.

say: Members join voluntarily, to meet real shared needs.

say: And it is a real business, owned together and governed by the members.

say: The seven principles put the values into practice. Membership is open, with written admission rules. And in primary cooperatives, it is one member, one vote, however many shares she holds.

panel.heading: How values become practice
items: Fair capital, surplus shared by use

say: Members contribute capital fairly. Surplus, the money left after costs, goes to reserves, to members according to their business with the cooperative, or to activities members approve.

panel.heading: How values become practice
items: Fair capital, surplus shared by use

say: Agreements with governments, buyers or funders must keep member control. For example, refuse a grant that would let the donor appoint your treasurer.

panel.heading: How values become practice
items: Fair capital, surplus shared by use

say: The last three: train members and leaders, work with other cooperatives, and serve your community.

panel.heading: How values become practice
items: Fair capital, surplus shared by use

say: For example, Bisola leads a 14-member sewing group in Ibadan. She scores each principle 2 if fully true, 1 if partly, 0 if not, out of 14.
New members join only if the founder likes them: 0. Officers were never elected, and the founder decides alone: 0.
Everyone paid the same 20,000 naira entry share, but surplus was never shared: 1. Two members learnt the machines, but nobody learnt bookkeeping: 1.
Autonomy, buying fabric with another group, and free uniform repairs for orphans score 2 each.
Total: 8 out of 14. Her weakest points are membership rules and democratic control, so her bylaws must fix admission and elections first.

panel.heading: Bisola scores her sewing group
panel.rule: Total: 8 out of 14. Fix membership and elections first.

say: An informal group is fine while money is small. But it is not a legal person. If the treasurer signs for a 2 million naira fabric order and the buyer cancels, the supplier can chase the treasurer personally.

panel.heading: Who carries the risk?
right: A legal entity owned by members

say: A cooperative society is registered with your state's cooperative office, not the Corporate Affairs Commission, and signs contracts in its own name.
Get current requirements and fees in writing from that office, and never pay an agent without an official receipt.

panel.heading: Who carries the risk?
right: A legal entity owned by members

say: Registration only gives trust a legal shape. So first score eight points: 2 if in place, 1 if partly, 0 if missing. Start with a written agreement, officers elected for a fixed term, and a group account needing two signatures.
Then a weekly cashbook, receipts for contributions, monthly meetings with minutes, an agreed way to settle disagreements, and a product with known costs.
Kemi's adire group in Abeokuta scored 10, because the money sat in the chairperson's personal account. So they spend about 90 days fixing gaps before registering.

panel.heading: Score readiness out of 16
panel.rule: 12 or more: go. 8 to 11: fix gaps for 90 days. Below 8: build.

say: Bylaws are the rule book. A quorum is the minimum number of members who must be present for decisions to count. Serious matters need a special resolution, often two-thirds.
For example, Ngozi is secretary of a 24-member palm oil cooperative near Owerri.

panel.heading: Quorum and a two-thirds vote
items: 24 members: quorum is half plus one, 13
Record it all in the minutes

say: Half of 24 is 12, plus one is 13. 18 members came, so quorum is met.

panel.heading: Quorum and a two-thirds vote
items: 24 members: quorum is half plus one, 13
Record it all in the minutes

say: Buying a press on credit is a special resolution. Two-thirds of 18 is 12. The vote is 13 yes, so it passes.

panel.heading: Quorum and a two-thirds vote
items: 24 members: quorum is half plus one, 13

say: Ngozi records members present, the motion and the vote count in the minutes.

say: These money rules prevent most quarrels. No officer keeps group money in a personal account. Two signatories, not from the same household, approve each payment. Set spending limits, and record every naira with a receipt.
Never share the banking PIN or one-time passwords in the WhatsApp group. Confirm unusual requests by calling a saved number.

panel.heading: Protect members' money
items: All money in the group bank account
Never share PINs or one-time passwords

say: To remember. One member, one vote. Score your group honestly against all seven principles. In an informal group, officers carry the risk personally.
When you are ready, register with your state's cooperative office, with bylaws that set quorum, voting and money rules.

items: One member, one vote, whatever her shares
